chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharjah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying at the end of his speech when he departed: 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from being unjust, or being treated unjustly, or cutting off a relationship, or harming a neighbour.'

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: To depart or disperse (specifically referring to the Prophet's or Imam's farewell sermon at Arafat)
key_terms.أَوْ أَقْطَعَ رَحِمًا: Or from cutting off kinship ties
key_terms.أَوْ أُظْلَمَ: Or from being treated unjustly (by others)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq say in his farewell supplication at Arafat?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this supplication highlights the Imam’s emphasis on social ethics during the pivotal moment of departing Arafat, a key rite of Hajj. It underscores the Shia scholarly focus on integrating personal piety with communal responsibilities, specifically seeking divine protection from five major social transgressions: oppression, being oppressed, severing kinship ties, and harming neighbors.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Usman Bin Isa, from Haroun Bin Kharjat who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying at the end of his<sup>asws</sup> speech, when he<sup>asws</sup> departed: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with You<sup>azwj</sup> from being unjust, of mistreating, or cutting off a relationship, or harming a neighbour’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-FIusayn ibn Sa‘id from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Harun ibn Kharijah who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, when departing ‘Arafat at the end of his words, ‘O Allah, I seek protection with You against my disappointing, mistreating or doing injustice to or being treated unjustly by a relative or a neighbor.’”
